name: Learn how to remember people’s names
blurb: Most people forget names because they never actually heard them. Four small habits fix nearly all of it, and the social return is large.
steps: Decide, before you are introduced, that you are going to learn the name. Almost all forgetting is inattention.
Repeat it immediately: “Good to meet you, Priya.” This confirms pronunciation and rehearses it.
Attach an image: link the name to a visual feature, a person you know with the same name, or an absurd association.
Use it again mid-conversation and once when you leave, spacing the repetitions.
Review names afterwards — a list on your phone after an event is not cheating.
When you forget, just ask. “I have lost your name, I am sorry” is far less awkward than avoiding them for a year.
tips: If you did not hear it clearly, ask right then. It is never easier later.
Names with unfamiliar sounds need one extra repetition, and getting them right matters more, not less.
proof: You meet ten new people at an event and can name eight of them an hour later.
